# Permissions

Who may do what to a file, in both spellings the supported systems use.

```rux
pub struct Permissions {
    pub mode: uint32;
    // private fields
}
```

`mode` is the Unix permission bits, the low nine of which are the owner/group/other triple. `readOnly` is
Windows' one portable attribute. Both are always filled: on Windows the mode is synthesized from the
attribute (`0o444` when read-only, `0o666` otherwise) so a program that reasons in Unix terms is not blocked,
and on Unix `readOnly` reports whether the owner-write bit is clear. [`Capabilities`](/docs/api/filesystem/capabilities) says which one is real.

## Related

<h3 id="set-permissions"><code>SetPermissions</code></h3>

```rux
pub func SetPermissions(
    allocator: Allocator,
    path: Path,
    permissions: Permissions
) -> ! IoError
```

Sets who may do what to the file `path` names.
On the Unix systems the mode bits are written as given. On Windows only the read-only attribute exists, so
that alone is written and the rest of `permissions` is ignored — ask [`CapabilitiesOfSystem`](/docs/api/filesystem/capabilities#capabilities-of-system) first if the
difference matters. A symbolic link is always followed: its own bits mean nothing on any supported system.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/FileSystem/Src/Metadata.rux#L417)

**Parameters**

| Name          | Type          | Description                  |
| ------------- | ------------- | ---------------------------- |
| `allocator`   | `Allocator`   | where the storage comes from |
| `path`        | `Path`        | the path to act on           |
| `permissions` | `Permissions` | the permissions to apply     |

**Returns**: success when the permissions were applied
